moves.name: Squash and stretch
moves.summary: An object flattens on impact and lengthens in fast travel while keeping its volume, so it reads as soft, alive and pulled by gravity.

moves.name: Anticipation
moves.summary: A small move in the opposite direction before the main action, like a crouch before a jump, so the viewer knows something is about to happen.

moves.name: Overshoot and settle
moves.summary: An element travels slightly past its resting place and eases back, giving arrivals a sense of momentum instead of a dead stop.

moves.name: Follow-through and overlapping action
moves.summary: Loose parts of an object start moving after the body and keep going after it stops, so a move reads as one physical thing instead of a rigid block.

moves.name: Spring animation
moves.summary: Motion driven by a damped spring instead of a fixed curve, tuned with stiffness, damping and mass, so arrivals feel physical and consistent.

moves.name: Staggered timing
moves.summary: A group of items runs the same animation with small start offsets, so the group arrives as one directional ripple instead of all at once.

moves.name: Slow in and slow out
moves.summary: A move starts gently, gathers speed in the middle and decelerates into its stop. The default for anything traveling between two on-screen points.

moves.name: Ease-out entrance
moves.summary: Elements arrive fast and decelerate into place, then leave by accelerating away, so entrances feel confident and exits get out of the way.

moves.name: Arcs
moves.summary: Moving objects follow curved paths rather than straight lines, the way thrown balls, swinging limbs and real hands on a mouse do.

moves.name: Moving hold
moves.summary: During a pause the frame keeps a trace of motion, like a 2 percent push-in or a slow drift, so a held moment never looks frozen.

moves.name: Secondary action
moves.summary: A smaller supporting motion that happens with the main one, like a blink during a hop or neighbors nudging aside when a card lands.

moves.name: Animating on twos
moves.summary: Each pose is held for two or more frames, giving smooth code-driven motion the stepped, hand-made cadence of cel animation or stop motion.

moves.name: Staggered letter reveal
moves.summary: A word appears one character at a time, each letter rising and fading in a few frames after the one before it, so the word ripples into place.

moves.name: Word by word reveal
aka: one word at a time text
moves.summary: A sentence builds one word at a time, each word rising out of a light blur into its final slot, paced to the voice or the beat.

moves.name: Typewriter text
moves.summary: Text types itself out character by character behind a caret, with an uneven human rhythm, like someone entering a prompt or a search query.

moves.name: Text scramble decode
moves.summary: Each letter flickers through random glyphs before locking onto the right character, left to right, so the word appears to decode itself.

moves.name: Line mask text reveal
moves.summary: Each line of text slides up from behind an invisible edge, as if rising out of a slot in the page, then stops dead on its baseline.

moves.name: Variable font weight animation
moves.summary: A word swells from hairline thin to heavy black (or back) by animating a variable font's weight axis, so the letters themselves change shape.

moves.name: Text on a path
moves.summary: A line of text runs along a curve, circle or wave and slides along it, so the words travel the shape like a train on a track.

moves.name: Rotating word swap
moves.summary: One word inside a fixed headline rolls vertically to the next option and the next, while the rest of the sentence stays perfectly still.

moves.name: Split-flap text
moves.summary: Letters flip like an old airport departure board, each tile rattling through the alphabet before it lands on the right character.

moves.name: Scale punch headline
moves.summary: A headline hits the screen oversized, snaps down past its final size and settles with a small spring, landing like a punch on the beat.

moves.name: Tracking expand title
moves.summary: A title fades in with its letters slowly drifting apart, letter-spacing easing from tight to wide over several seconds, like a film opening.

moves.name: Outline to fill text
moves.summary: Letters first draw themselves as thin outlines, then fill in with solid colour, so a word goes from blueprint to finished type.

moves.name: Match cut
moves.summary: A hard cut between two shots that share a shape, color or position, so the eye carries straight across and the change feels intended.

moves.name: Whip pan transition
moves.summary: The outgoing shot snaps sideways into a directional blur and the next shot decelerates in from the same direction, hiding the cut in the smear.

moves.name: Wipe transition
moves.summary: A moving edge sweeps across the frame, revealing the next shot behind it, often with a thin accent-colored line leading the reveal.

moves.name: Iris transition
moves.summary: A circle or aperture closes down on a point of the frame and opens again onto the next shot, centred on the same spot.

moves.name: Morph transition
moves.summary: One element persists across two scenes and glides from its old size, position and color into its new one while the rest of the scene changes around it.

moves.name: Color flood transition
moves.summary: A shape grows out of an element in the frame until its color covers the screen, then becomes the next scene's background or shrinks into its next element.

moves.name: Zoom-through transition
moves.summary: The camera pushes into a detail with accelerating scale until it fills the frame, then the next scene settles in from inside it.

moves.name: Push transition
moves.summary: The outgoing shot slides off one edge while the incoming shot slides on behind it, both moving together like pages on a strip.

moves.name: Cross-dissolve
moves.summary: Two shots overlap in opacity so one fades through the other, signaling passing time or a change of mood rather than a jump.

moves.name: Glitch cut
moves.summary: One or two frames of digital breakup, like channel split, slice offsets or pixel smear, sit exactly on a cut so the change feels like signal interference.

moves.name: Light leak transition
moves.summary: A warm wash of overexposed color blooms across the frame, peaks over the cut point, and fades to reveal the next shot, like light hitting film.

moves.name: J-cut and L-cut
moves.summary: The sound of the next scene starts before its picture (J-cut), or the current scene's sound continues after the picture changes (L-cut).

moves.name: Cursor-led product demo
moves.summary: A synthetic cursor glides across a recreated interface, pauses, clicks and drives each state change so the viewer follows one point of attention.

moves.name: Click ripple
moves.summary: On click, the button dips slightly and a soft ring expands from the exact press point and fades, confirming the interaction.

moves.name: Auto zoom on click
moves.summary: The whole interface scales up toward the area being used, follows the cursor while it works, then eases back out to show context.

moves.name: Card stack
moves.summary: Cards arrive one after another and settle on top of each other with a small offset, shrink and dim, building a layered pile with depth.

moves.name: Modal spring-in
moves.summary: A dialog scales up from slightly smaller with a light spring overshoot while the background dims and blurs behind it.

moves.name: Skeleton to content
moves.summary: Grey placeholder blocks shimmer in the shape of a layout, then real text and images fade in over them block by block.

moves.name: Toast notification
moves.summary: A small notification slides in from a screen edge with a quick spring, holds long enough to read, then slides or shrinks away.

moves.name: Tab indicator slide
moves.summary: The active tab underline or pill glides to the newly selected tab, stretching as it travels, then snaps to the new width.

moves.name: UI number ticker
moves.summary: A number inside the interface counts or rolls to its new value, digit columns spinning like an odometer, then settles.

moves.name: Scroll-through screen
moves.summary: A long page or app screen scrolls past inside a frame with eased momentum, stopping on key sections before moving on.

moves.name: Device frame reveal
moves.summary: The shot starts full-screen on the UI, then pulls back as a phone or laptop bezel grows around it, placing the app in a device.

moves.name: UI state morph
moves.summary: One shape flows through a chain of interface states, button to loader to check to slider to toast, without ever cutting.

moves.name: Path draw-on
moves.summary: A vector stroke draws itself along its path from start to end, as if an invisible pen were tracing the shape in real time.

moves.name: Shape morph
moves.summary: One vector shape smoothly turns into another, its outline flowing from circle to square to whatever comes next without a cut.

moves.name: Vector mask reveal
moves.summary: Content appears through a growing vector shape used as a mask, so the image or scene is revealed in the silhouette of that shape.

moves.name: Gooey split and merge
moves.summary: Shapes pull apart and fuse like drops of liquid, stretching a bridge between them before they snap into separate blobs or one.

moves.name: Trim path loop
moves.summary: A stroke segment chases itself around a path: its head and tail move at different speeds, so the line grows, shrinks and loops forever.

moves.name: Icon morph
moves.summary: A small icon transforms into its next state, like play into pause or menu into close, with its strokes rotating and reshaping in place.

moves.name: Geometric pattern build
moves.summary: A geometric pattern assembles step by step from simple primitives, with lines, circles and polygons appearing in a precise construction order.

moves.name: Isometric build
moves.summary: Flat isometric blocks, buildings or devices assemble piece by piece, dropping and extruding into place on a 30-degree grid.

moves.name: Radial burst
moves.summary: Short lines or shapes shoot outward from a single point in a ring, flaring and fading in a fraction of a second to mark an impact.

moves.name: Orbiting shapes
moves.summary: Small shapes, icons or words circle a central element on elliptical paths, giving a hub-and-satellites loop that never stops moving.

moves.name: Grid tessellation
moves.summary: A surface fills with repeating tiles such as squares, triangles or hexagons that appear, flip or rotate in waves across the grid.

moves.name: Shard assemble
moves.summary: Faceted polygon shards fly in from around the frame and lock together, one by one, until they form a complete logo or object.

moves.name: Particle assemble
moves.summary: Thousands of scattered particles fly in and settle into a logo, word or image, or break apart from it and drift away.

moves.name: Flow field
moves.summary: Particles drift along an invisible current defined by noise, leaving soft streaks that look like wind, smoke or iron filings.

moves.name: Noise displacement
moves.summary: Coherent noise pushes vertices or pixels around over time, so a flat shape, grid or surface ripples and breathes like something alive.

moves.name: Instanced grid
moves.summary: A large grid of identical dots, tiles or cubes where every cell reacts to one shared field, producing ripples, waves and shapes that sweep across.

moves.name: L-system growth
moves.summary: Lines branch and split from a single seed point into a tree, root network or vein pattern that grows across the frame over time.

moves.name: Flocking boids
moves.summary: Many small agents steer by three simple rules, separation, alignment and cohesion, so they move together like a flock of birds or a school of fish.

moves.name: Voronoi cells
moves.summary: The frame splits into organic cells around moving seed points, with borders that shift and redraw as the points drift, like foam, cracked mud or stained glass.

moves.name: Reaction-diffusion
moves.summary: Two simulated chemicals spread and react to grow labyrinths, spots and coral-like stripes that slowly fill the frame from a seed.

moves.name: Metaballs
moves.summary: Soft round blobs drift and, when close, stretch and fuse into one gooey surface, then neck and split apart again like a lava lamp.

moves.name: Ordered dither
moves.summary: Images, gradients or 3D renders reduced to a small set of colors through a fixed threshold pattern, giving a crisp 1-bit, retro-print look.

moves.name: Attractor trails
moves.summary: Points follow the equations of a strange attractor, tracing glowing ribbons that loop around invisible centers without ever repeating.

moves.name: Infinite fractal zoom
moves.summary: The camera dives into a self-similar shape forever: every level reveals the same pattern again, so the zoom loops seamlessly.

moves.name: Dolly in
moves.summary: The whole frame moves steadily closer to the subject, so attention narrows onto one thing without a cut.

moves.name: Breathing push
moves.summary: A barely visible, continuous push of 2 to 4 percent during a hold that keeps a static frame feeling alive.

moves.name: Punch in
moves.summary: A sudden 4 to 8 frame jump in framing, tighter on the subject, used to hit a beat or a key word.

moves.name: Crash zoom
moves.summary: A violent, very fast zoom from wide to tight with motion blur, used for comedy, shock or a hard reveal.

moves.name: Pull back reveal
moves.summary: The camera pulls away from a detail to show the larger scene it belongs to, turning a close-up into context.

moves.name: Parallax layers
moves.summary: Foreground, midground and background move at different speeds as the camera travels, creating depth from flat layers.

moves.name: Camera orbit
moves.summary: The camera circles around a subject on an arc, revealing its sides and depth while keeping it centered.

moves.name: Rack focus
moves.summary: Focus shifts from one layer to another: the old subject softens into blur while the new one sharpens.

moves.name: Camera shake
moves.summary: The frame jitters with decaying, seeded noise for a few frames after an impact, or drifts gently like a handheld camera.

moves.name: Dolly zoom
moves.summary: The subject holds its size while the background stretches or compresses behind it, creating an uneasy shift in space.

moves.name: 2.5D camera projection
moves.summary: A still image is split into depth layers or mapped onto depth, so a virtual camera can move through it with real parallax.

moves.name: Overhead fly-over
moves.summary: The camera glides low over a surface, then rises to a straight-down overhead view that shows the whole layout at once.

moves.name: Film grain
moves.summary: A fine layer of monochrome noise, regenerated every frame, that makes flat vector or UI frames feel shot rather than exported.

moves.name: Chromatic aberration
moves.summary: Red and blue channels drift a pixel or two apart toward the frame edges, giving a lens-like color fringe on high-contrast shapes.

moves.name: Halftone
moves.summary: Tone is drawn as a grid of dots whose size follows brightness, giving a printed, comic-book or newspaper finish that can animate.

moves.name: Glow and bloom
moves.summary: Bright parts of the frame bleed a soft halo of light into their surroundings, so the lead element looks lit rather than drawn.

moves.name: Paper texture
moves.summary: A visible paper surface with fibers and tooth sits under the artwork, and ink or color sits in it, so the film reads as made by hand.

moves.name: CRT scanlines
moves.summary: Thin dark horizontal lines, a slight screen curve and a soft phosphor glow make the frame look like it is playing on an old tube monitor.

moves.name: Mesh gradient
moves.summary: Several soft color points drift slowly under a background, blending into a smooth, shifting field of color that never quite repeats.

moves.name: Risograph print
moves.summary: Two or three flat spot-color inks overlap with grainy fills and a slight misregistration, like a small-run risograph poster.

moves.name: Light sweep
moves.summary: A narrow band of light slides across a logo, card or button once, as if it caught a reflection, then the surface settles back.

moves.name: Motion blur
moves.summary: Fast-moving elements smear along their path within each frame, the way a camera shutter records them, so quick moves look smooth instead of strobing.

moves.name: Ink bleed
moves.summary: Ink or paint spreads from a point into the paper with ragged, feathered edges, revealing an image or shape the way wet media soaks in.

moves.name: Grainy gradient
moves.summary: A soft color gradient carries visible noise so it looks tactile and printed, and so it survives video compression without banding.

moves.name: Bar chart race
moves.summary: Horizontal bars grow and swap rank over time while a large date counter ticks, showing who leads and when the lead changes.

moves.name: Line chart draw-on
moves.summary: A chart line draws itself from left to right with a glowing head, so the viewer follows the trend as it happens instead of seeing it all at once.

moves.name: Counter roll-up
moves.summary: A big number counts up from zero and decelerates onto its final value, often with a small punch when it lands.

moves.name: Donut chart sweep
moves.summary: Donut or pie segments sweep around the circle one after another, each settling into its share while the percentage counts beside it.

moves.name: Map route draw
moves.summary: A route line draws across a map from origin to destination, with a marker leading the line and the camera following the journey.

moves.name: Dot swarm chart
moves.summary: Many small dots, one per unit, fly from a loose cloud into a grid, cluster or scatter plot, so quantities become something you can count.

moves.name: Highlight one bar
moves.summary: After a chart builds, every bar fades to grey except one, which takes the accent color and a label, telling the viewer exactly where to look.

moves.name: Axis and grid reveal
moves.summary: The chart frame builds before the data: axes extend from the origin, gridlines draw across in a quick stagger, and tick labels fade in.

moves.name: Stacked area grow
moves.summary: Layered areas rise from the baseline one band at a time, each stacking on the last, so the viewer sees both the total and its parts.

moves.name: Annotation callout
moves.summary: A leader line draws out from a data point and a short label pops in at its end, pointing the viewer to the one detail that matters.

moves.name: Sankey flow
moves.summary: Bands of varying width flow from sources to destinations, drawing left to right so the viewer sees where every share of a total goes.

moves.name: Before and after data split
moves.summary: Two states of the same chart or metric share the frame, split by a divider that slides across to reveal the change from before to after.

moves.name: Beat-synced cuts
moves.summary: Scene changes land exactly on the music's downbeats, so the edit feels played by the track instead of laid over it.

moves.name: BPM grid timing
moves.summary: All motion durations are written in beats rather than seconds, so every move starts and ends on the song's tempo grid.

moves.name: Kick pulse
moves.summary: An element punches up in scale on every kick drum and eases back before the next one, like it is being pushed by the bass.

moves.name: Waveform visualizer
moves.summary: A line traces the actual shape of the audio, scrolling or redrawing each frame so the sound becomes visible.

moves.name: Frequency bars
moves.summary: A row of bars rises and falls with the music's frequency content, bass on one side and treble on the other.

moves.name: Lyric sync
moves.summary: Each word of the lyrics appears or highlights exactly when it is sung, timed to the vocal rather than to a guess.

moves.name: Sound-reactive particles
moves.summary: A particle field breathes with the music: bass pushes it outward, highs add sparkle, and the drop throws it apart.

moves.name: Hit frames on transients
moves.summary: Every visible contact, landing or click shares its exact frame with the peak of its sound, so picture and audio feel like one event.

moves.name: Silence before the drop
moves.summary: Sound cuts out and the picture freezes or empties for a beat or two, so the next hit lands twice as hard.

moves.name: Riser build
moves.summary: Over the bars leading into a drop, motion speeds up, the camera pushes in and the frame tightens until the drop releases it.

moves.name: Sidechain pump
moves.summary: Background layers dip in brightness or scale on every kick and swell back between them, mirroring the pumping sound of dance music.

moves.name: Stinger sync
moves.summary: A short, distinct sound plays with a logo lockup so the final frame and the sound resolve together as one signature.
